messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.content:
The standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample mean (i.e., the standard error under the null hypothesis) is calculated as:

\[
SE = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}} = \frac{1.4}{\sqrt{40}} \approx \frac{1.4}{6.3249} \approx 0.2215
\]

So the standard deviation of the null‑hypothesis test is **approximately 0.22**.
message.reasoning:
The user says: "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6."

They want the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test? That likely refers to the standard error of the mean under null hypothesis? The standard error = sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). But they mention population mean 98.6. The standard deviation of the null hypothesis test might be the standard error of the difference between sample mean and population mean? Actually, the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample mean under null is sigma/sqrt(n). If we don't know population sigma, we use sample sigma. So standard error = 1.4 / sqrt(40) ≈ 1.4 / 6.3249 ≈ 0.2215. So answer ~0.2215.

Alternatively, if they want the standard deviation of the test statistic? The test statistic t = (sample_mean - population_mean) / (sample_std_dev / sqrt(n)). The denominator is the standard error. So the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test is the standard error. So answer ~0.2215.

Thus we can compute. Let's do calculation: sqrt(40)=6.3249. 1.4/6.3249=0.2215. So answer: about 0.2215.

We can also mention that this is the standard error of the mean. So answer: 0.2215.
